It wasn't until the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965, however, that Minnesota officially opened its doors to Indians. From 1965 through the early 1990s, many came for higher degrees and eventually settled into largely professional jobs. In the later 1990s and early 2000s, a technology boom and temporary visas for skilled labor brought hundreds of thousands of Indians; some of them eventually settled in Minnesota. This surge encouraged businesses such as grocery stores and restaurants to open and led to the establishment of new organizations and services. The Indian American population in Minnesota has grown steadily, doubling every ten years since 1980.
